doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Exhausted at the Bill Conti Olympic session with Chuck Findley
summary: After a week of Jarreau nights, Hey recalls Chuck Findley's flawless trumpet solo at the 1984 Olympic music session.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: ahead of time and so you know we’re booked on other sessions from nine o’clock in the morning ‘til six at night, you know playing on these, whatever TV movies and everything. And then we’d go to the Jarreau session and start at eleven and go ‘til six or seven. Literally go home, take a shower, go to the nine o’clock or ten o’clock session. And we did that for a week for the Jarreau stuff. And on the fifth day, the Friday of that week, we had a nine o’clock call with Bill Conti for the 1984 Olympic music. And literally I’d had thirteen hours of sleep that week. And we go to this session, and we just got through with some brutal Jarreau stuff, you know one of those crazy ridiculously hard songs you know. And so you’ve got time to go home, take a shower, maybe get something to eat, nine o’clock session. And it’s six trumpets. So I got there pretty early but not early enough to get the sixth trumpet book. I could only get the fourth trumpet book. Gary Grant beat me to the sixth trumpet book. Chuck Findley comes in at one minute to nine o’clock, hair wet, obviously he hadn’t — he came directly from home, walks in and it’s like [motions strings playing] and trumpet like solo over the strings, like bravura Olympic music trumpet solo. And then four pages of, you know, playing and then at the end it’s the same thing, you know trumpet solo on strings. And he played the living hell out of it. And at that point I was lucky to even play. I was just shot. And so the rundown he played it perfectly. One take, great, and a viola player — “I think I have a wrong note.” And yes there was a wrong note and we had to do it again, and Chuck played it better the next time. It was amazing. That was kind of like the Chuck Findley that you always have heard about, and his legacy. It was incredible because if I were in that situation I couldn’t have played it.
It was one of those rare moments that you go okay, that is some sheer genius there, to be able to pull that off.
